sn10.1:1.2: The _yakkha_ Indaka is named after the mountain he inhabits. The mountain itself might be identified with Mount Vediyaka, where Sakka/Indra appeared to the Buddha at Indra’s hill cave ([dn21:1.1.2]()).
sn10.1:2.1: While this exact wording (_rūpaṁ na jīvan_) doesn’t seem to be a direct quote of the Buddha, it is a similar to _taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ_, which the Buddha did indeed deny. Taken by itself, of course, this does not deny that there *is* a soul, only that it is not physical. The use of _jīva_ for soul, rather than _attā_, is characteristic of the Jains, but is used by Vedists as well.
sn10.1:2.3: Perhaps “organs” would be better for _yakapiṇḍa_ here.
sn10.1:2.4: I disagree with BB’s reading of sajjati. The Skt root that he accepts, sṛj, rendered as “begotten”, has the basic meaning of “emit, discharge”. It’s attested in the context of procreation in the Rg Veda, where presumably it refers to the emission of semen. However the verses below are not concerned to answer the question of how procreation happens, but of how an embryo grows in the womb. I.e. not about “emission” but about “sticking around”.
sn10.1:3.2: “Cyst” is _abbuda_, otherwise used of a tumor or cancer. For other meanings, see notes on [sn1.77:1.4]() and [snp3.10:8.2]().
